nodes.description: NUBPL is an iron-sulfur cluster assembly factor for complex I. Analysis of how mutant NUBPL affects assembly of the peripheral arm placed its role early in the complex I assembly pathway, at the stage where iron-sulfur clusters are inserted. The peripheral arm is the electron-transferring limb of the complex, so a cluster-insertion failure there prevents the holoenzyme being completed rather than degrading an assembled enzyme's performance.

nodes.description: Complex I is the entry point of the respiratory chain, transferring electrons from NADH to ubiquinone while pumping protons. With the holoenzyme depleted, oxidative phosphorylation capacity falls. In patient fibroblasts the measurable consequence is significantly reduced spare respiratory capacity - the reserve a cell can call on above baseline demand - which is why tissues with high and fluctuating energy demand are affected first.

nodes.description: Biallelic NUBPL variants reduce functional NUBPL protein. The recurrent allele is the branch-site variant c.815-27T>C, present in all reported families and in roughly 1.2% of European haplotypes, which produces a frameshifted, altered C-terminus. Modelling that altered C-terminus in the yeast homologue Ind1 showed the mechanism is protein instability rather than transcript loss: mRNA was unaffected while protein level fell. Not every missense allele is equally damaging - p.Leu104Pro impaired complex I function in the yeast model while p.Val182Ala did not.
